title: UNIT 2 — AMITOSIS (Direct Cell Division)
source: Biology Units 1to5 Conceptual Study Notes — UNIT 2 — AMITOSIS (Direct Cell Division), pages 4-4 [Biology_Units_1to5_Conceptual_Study_Notes.docx]
textbookText: Amitosis is the simplest type of cell division. The word means 'without mitosis' (a = without, mitosis = mitosis). The nucleus just splits into two and the cell pinches into two — no fancy structures, no visible chromosomes, no spindle fibres. It is also called 'direct division' because the nucleus divides straight into two with no middle steps.
Step 1 — The nucleus grows longer (like a dumbbell).
Step 2 — It pinches into two equal halves.
Step 3 — The whole cell splits, giving two daughter cells that look almost exactly like the parent.

It's fast and cheap, but the two daughters are almost identical copies and it offers no way to mix genes or fix errors. It's mostly used in one-celled organisms (like amoeba and some parasites) and rarely in normal human cells.
No preparation, no line-up, no spindle — just snap in two. Mitosis and meiosis are the hard-working ones; amitosis is the lazy one.
